title: Fix the "Edit this page on GitHub" link in Vitepress documentation for the Mermaid Config pages
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Fix the "Edit this page on GitHub" link for the Mermaid Config Schema http://localhost:3333/config/schema-docs/config.html.

### Before (edit link points to file that doesn't exist)

Edit Link points to `packages/mermaid/src/docs/config/schema-docs/config.md`, **which doesn't exist**: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/edit/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs/config/schema-docs/config.md

![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/66b36d88-03fa-4d2e-8d0c-a89c73730506)

### After (edit link points to correct file)

Edit Link correctly points to `packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml`: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/edit/develop/packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml

![image](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/assets/19716675/a0cc9517-7df3-4575-b9b9-3ad031e53ac5)

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

[Vitepress 1.0.0-beta.53](https://github.com/vuejs/vitepress/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#100-alpha53-2023-03-13) allowed the `editLink` parameter in the Vitepress config to accept a function, instead of just a pattern. I've changed this Vitepress config function to then accept a custom edit link in the YAML frontmatter of Markdown files, which is created by `transformMarkdownAst`.

So essentially:
  - `transformMarkdownAst({originalFilename, addEditLink: true})` now adds the following YAML frontmatter to a markdown file:
    ```markdown
    ---
    editLink: "https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/edit/develop/packages/mermaid/src/schemas/config.schema.yaml"
    ---
    
    Here is my markdown file!
    ```
  - Our custom `.vitepress/config.ts` `editLink.pattern` function will then use the `frontmatter.editLink` as the edit link, if it exists.
   

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added unit/e2e tests (if appropriate)
- [x] :notebook: have added documentation (if appropriate)
- [x] :bookmark: targeted `develop` branch

comments.body:
> Edit: I just now notice the +=. This is not safe.

:facepalm: I should have realized that! Thanks for the catch!

It's not part of a public API, it's only used to create some YAML frontmatter keys in our documentation folder: https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/tree/develop/packages/mermaid/src/docs. But still, it's better to do it properly now, so we can avoid future bugs.

I've fixed this in https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/pull/4640/commits/4d2d790cc8de03adde3fb5b820e1da7f4fd29bae. I know you recommended using [`yaml`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/yaml), but since we've already got [`js-yaml`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/js-yaml) as a `devDependency`, I've gone ahead and reused the same package. (maybe it's worth replacing `js-yaml` completely with `yaml` in another PR, though) We were even using `js-yaml` in the same file that I edited.

I've given you `Reported-by: ` credit in a git commit message, but my patch is pretty similar to your proposed patch, so I'd be happy to give you a [`Co-authored-by: `](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/committing-changes-to-your-project/creating-and-editing-commits/creating-a-commit-with-multiple-authors) credit too :smile:
